$comment: PERMISSIONS PROFILE FOR THE LAYER 2 WEEKLY AUTONOMOUS RUN — loaded with
`claude -p --settings .claude/weekly-autonomous.settings.json --permission-prompts none`.
DENY-BY-DEFAULT. Nothing here grants a shell; `allow` lists command PREFIXES and
anything unmatched is refused outright because --permission-prompts none turns a
would-be prompt into a denial. Nobody is awake to answer one.
DENY BEATS ALLOW, and that is the load-bearing property: --settings is ADDITIVE to
the operator's own settings, so `allow` alone could be widened from outside this
file. The `deny` list cannot be.
WHY EACH ALLOW EXISTS — read before widening:
express 'read-only' for an arbitrary inner command, so the inner
command is pinned instead of the flag.
the whole tree and reached 18 GB / OOM; the anchor makes the
unscoped form unmatchable rather than merely discouraged.
git           fetch/status/log/merge-base/rebase/push PLUS add/commit/diff/show,
because §3 of the prompt pre-authorizes MERGES and a unit that
cannot commit cannot complete one.
curl          host-pinned to the Discord webhook prefix. The capability exists to
satisfy the brief; it is unusable in practice because the webhook
token is cleared from the environment before claude is launched.
MEASURED 2026-09-14 against Claude Code 2.1.270 — a Bash prefix rule matches at WHOLE-TOKEN
boundaries, so `Bash(python -m pytest tests/test_:*)` did NOT match a real named-file run and
`Bash(railway ssh --service web "/opt/...:*)` cannot match inside a quoted argument. Both
constraints therefore live in tools/weekly_exec.py, which is allowed here and whose raw
equivalents (railway ssh, pytest) are DENIED above. Rail: tests/test_weekly_exec.py.
TRANSITIVE TRUST, STATED ON PURPOSE: allow-listing `python tools/<x>.py` grants whatever
that tool does, including any subprocess it starts. flag_ledger_audit.py shells `railway
variables` internally - which is DENIED to the model directly and reachable through this
tool. That is accepted because the tool is read-only by construction; it is NOT a licence
to allow-list a tool that writes.
